memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I will put my dwelling place among you, and I will not abhor you. I
will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people'"
- Lev 26:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the summit of the entire chapter. After all the promises of
harvest, safety and victory, God gives the greatest gift of all: I will
dwell among you. I will walk among you. I will be your God, and you will
be my people.

This is the language of intimacy. God does not merely visit; He moves in.
He does not remain distant; He walks among His people as a companion. This
was always the deepest purpose of the covenant — not just to bless Israel,
but to be with them.

Dear reader, this promise runs like a golden thread through the whole
Bible, gathering strength as it goes. It began in Eden, where God walked
with man in the garden. It took shape in the tabernacle. And it reached
its fullness when the Word became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14).

Paul quotes these very verses and applies them to the church: we are the
temple of the living God, as God has said, I will live with them and walk
among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people (2 Cor
6:16).

And the story is not finished. John saw the final vision: God's dwelling
place is now among the people, and He will dwell with them (Rev 21:3).

The whole Bible is moving towards God dwelling with His people forever. In
Christ, that dwelling has already begun in you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live conscious that God dwells with me, not far off?
2. What does it mean that God wants to walk with me, not just bless me?
3. How does the promise of God dwelling with us forever shape my hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your deepest desire is to dwell among Your people.
Thank You that in Christ You walk with me now, and one day will dwell with
me forever. Amen.
